subject: combining distance and removal data in Program Distance

messages.author: 4e22b0c52904009c
messages.subject: combining distance and removal data in Program Distance
parts:
I have data from a survey where we collected distances to each bird detec=
ted
and the 2-minute interval in which the bird was first detected (for a
removal model). Is there a way to enter both types of data into Program
Distance to combine the two approaches? Or do I have to enter the removal=

data in a separate program (like Capture) and combine the results after t=
he
individual analyses? From what I've seen so far, there does not seem to b=
e a
way to combine the two types of data in Program Distance in its current
version, but I just wanted to make sure. Any help would be appreciated.

Vicki Garcia

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: combining distance and removal data in Program Distance
parts:
Vicki-

Your assessment is correct. There is no facility for this in Distance.
In some ways this is similar to the last posting but would
be handled differently in the analysis and would most likely involve
more than 2 occasions. I'm not a big fan of the approach you are using
because it ignores movement which could lead to substantial positive
bias. But that said, you can proceed by using a removal model
in MARK to estimate g(0) and then enter that with its std error into
Distance. Just as with the last post, this works as long as there are
no additional covariates like species, habitat etc that affect g(0). If
you do have that situation then you would need to stratify your distance
data
and do separate analysis with separate g(0) values.

regards --jeff
